blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Financial analysis at the rise level is the craft of turning numbers into decisions. A good analyst does not just present a pile of figures; they tell the story the figures are telling, recommend an action, and explain what would have to be true for the action to succeed. That shape — story, recommendation, condition — is what turns analysis into a useful conversation.

The mistake most analysts make is to stop at the numbers. "Here is the data; you decide" sounds humble, but it is not what the business needs. The business needs: "Here is what I see. Here is what I would do. Here is the one thing that would make me change my mind."

Decisions rarely fail for lack of data. They fail for lack of someone willing to put a clear recommendation next to the data and stand behind it.

items.q: According to the text, what is financial analysis at the rise level?
options: The practice of collecting as much data as possible
The craft of turning numbers into decisions
A way of avoiding responsibility for decisions
The presentation of figures without any comment
items.why: "Financial analysis at the rise level is the craft of turning numbers into decisions."

items.q: What three-part shape turns analysis into a useful conversation?
options: Story, recommendation, condition
Data, chart, summary
Problem, budget, deadline
Question, answer, review
items.why: "That shape — story, recommendation, condition — is what turns analysis into a useful conversation."

items.q: According to the text, why do decisions usually fail?
options: Because there is too much data to read
For lack of someone willing to recommend and stand behind it
Because analysts disagree with each other
Because the data is inaccurate
items.why: "They fail for lack of someone willing to put a clear recommendation next to the data and stand behind it."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Naming a condition strengthens an analysis
A recommendation is more valuable than a pile of figures
Saying 'you decide' is the most professional way to present analysis
An analyst should say what they would do, not just what the data shows
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que "you decide" soa humilde mas não é o que o negócio precisa — o autor discordaria de tratá-lo como o mais profissional.

items.q: What does the phrase "the one thing that would make me change my mind" suggest about a good recommendation?
options: It should hide any weaknesses in the analysis
It should never be questioned once made
It is stronger when the analyst is honest about its main risk
It should be made only when the data is complete
items.why: Inferência: nomear a condição que mudaria a opinião mostra honestidade sobre o principal risco, o que reforça a recomendação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James orientando um novo analista depois de uma reunião. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Can I be honest with you? Those were the cleanest slides I have seen all quarter. The numbers were right, the charts were readable, and the room went completely quiet — and then nothing happened. That is the problem I want to talk about.

You ended on the data. "Here are the figures." And you sat down. So everyone looked at each other, nobody wanted to be the first to commit, and the decision just drifted to next week's meeting. Beautiful analysis, zero movement.

Next time, I want one more slide. After the numbers, tell me what you would actually do. Not five options — one recommendation, in a sentence. Then tell me the single thing that would make you change your mind. That last part is not weakness; it is what earns you trust in the room.

You are worried that if the call turns out wrong, it lands on you. It will. That is the job. But a room will forgive an analyst who was clear and stood behind a view far sooner than one who hid behind the data and let the business stall.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James say happened after the analyst presented the slides?
options: The room asked many detailed questions
The numbers were found to be wrong
The board approved the plan at once
The room went quiet and then nothing happened
items.why: "the room went completely quiet — and then nothing happened."

items.q: What extra slide does James want next time?
options: A slide listing the sources of the figures
A slide with one recommendation and the thing that would change his mind
A slide with five different options to choose from
A slide summarising all the data again
items.why: "one recommendation, in a sentence. Then tell me the single thing that would make you change your mind."

items.q: How does James describe naming the thing that would change your mind?
options: A weakness to be avoided
An optional detail for junior analysts
A way to delay the decision
Something that earns you trust in the room
items.why: "That last part is not weakness; it is what earns you trust in the room."

items.q: What can we infer James means by "Beautiful analysis, zero movement"?
options: The charts should have used more colour
Good-looking work is worthless if it leads to no decision
The meeting ran out of time
The analysis was too short to be useful
items.why: Inferência: por mais limpa que fosse a análise, sem recomendação ela não gerou nenhuma decisão.

items.q: What does James suggest about the risk of being wrong?
options: It comes with the job, and clarity earns more forgiveness than hiding
It is better to hide behind the data than to be blamed
Being wrong is unacceptable and ends careers
The analyst should avoid making any call to escape blame
items.why: Inferência: ele admite que o erro recai sobre o analista ("That is the job"), mas diz que a sala perdoa mais quem foi claro do que quem se escondeu nos dados.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Turning numbers into decisions is a craft, not a formula." Here craft means…
options: a quick shortcut
a written report
a piece of software
a skilled practice you develop over time
items.why: Craft = ofício: uma prática habilidosa que se apura com o tempo.

items.q: "She refused to hand the board a pile of figures with no direction." A pile of figures is…
options: a mass of numbers without interpretation
a clear recommendation
a signed approval
a single key metric
items.why: Pile of figures = monte de números — dados sem interpretação nem conclusão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He gave the data but no ___, so the meeting could not decide anything."
options: audience
recommendation
deadline
spreadsheet
items.why: Recommendation = recomendação — o que faltava para a reunião decidir.

items.q: "A good analyst names the one condition that would change the call." A condition here is…
options: a factor that would have to be true for the plan to hold
a formal contract clause
the health of the company
the state of the market
items.why: Condition = condição: aquilo que precisaria ser verdade para a recomendação se sustentar.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "She was ready to ___ her forecast even when the CFO challenged it."
options: sign off on
step back from
change her mind about
stand behind
items.why: To stand behind = defender, bancar — sustentar a previsão mesmo sob pressão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre análise e decisão. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The director asked the analyst to sign off on the final figures." To sign off on means to…
options: rewrite from scratch
formally approve
question informally
postpone indefinitely
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "He built a strong case but never followed through with a recommendation." This means he…
options: failed to take it to its conclusion
changed the case halfway
carried it all the way to completion
delegated it to the CFO
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim — aqui ele NÃO fechou com a recomendação.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the analyst's forecast." They…
options: copied it into their own report
approved it at once
presented it to the board
resisted or challenged it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Another pile of figures will not move the needle on this decision." This means it will…
options: cost too much to prepare
confuse the finance team
not make a noticeable difference
take longer than expected
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não fará.

items.q: "Let's zero in on the one assumption that decides the whole case." To zero in on means to…
options: remove entirely
postpone until later
argue against
focus closely on
items.why: Zero in on = concentrar-se em, mirar exatamente — focar na suposição decisiva.
